name: NOvA
summary: NOvA is an off-axis, long-baseline experiment measuring muon-flavour disappearance and electron-flavour appearance in neutrino and antineutrino beams from Fermilab.
physics_targets: Neutrino mass ordering and leptonic CP phase
Atmospheric mixing parameters and electron-flavour appearance
Neutrino cross sections, exotic interactions and supernova signals
detection_principle: Two functionally similar detectors contain liquid scintillator in highly segmented PVC cells. Wavelength-shifting fibres carry light to avalanche photodiodes. Long tracks and electromagnetic showers identify muon and electron charged-current interactions.

results.summary: Combined information with T2K in a joint oscillation fit, improving consistency checks across different baselines, energies and detector technologies.

The first joint NOvA-T2K fit sharpened oscillation constraints but found no strong preference for either mass ordering. Its CP-violation interpretation is conditional on the ordering and the three-flavour framework.
